question.leadin: Also known as Henry Bolingbroke, this man became King of England after deposing Richard II in 1399.
question.text: Identify this English king who was later succeeded by his son upon his 1413 death.
question.clue: During his last days, his court was split between factions loyal to his successor and those loyal to Thomas Arundel, archbishop of Canterbury.

swap.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
swap.text: The "first German to be called emperor of Italy," this man solidified his power by defeating the Magyars at Lechfeld and the Obodrites at Recknitz and established the Holy Roman Empire.
swap.clue: Much of his ruling strength came from his namesake system of installing his own bishops, and later in his rule, he deposed John XII in favor of Leo VIII for the papacy.

question.text: The Battles of Breitenfeld and Lutzen were victories for the Protestant States over the Catholics in this war, which was ended by the Peace of Westphalia. This war is named for its duration.
question.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

swap.leadin: Name these things associated with the Crusades.
swap.text: This man, known as "red beard" drowned in a river while on the way to fight Saladin.
swap.clue: This man crossed the Saleph River to participate in a conflict he organized with Philip Augustus and Richard the Lionheart.

question.text: Turgut Reis, a successor to this Muslim pirate, advised the Turks on how to capture the citadels during the siege. This corsair won the Battle of Preveza over the navy of Charles V and conquered Tunisia.
question.clue: Besides the pirate rulers of Algiers, Oruc and Hayreddin, another man with this epithet held a notable Diet at Besancon partially to legitimize his second marriage to Beatrice after his divorce from Adelheide.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the "first" Holy Roman Emperors.
swap.text: This man was the first to be crowned holy roman emperor in 962. He founded his dynasty after defeating the Magyars [MU-jars] in the battle of Lechfeld [LEK-feld].
swap.clue: He subjugated Berengar of Ivrea to rescue the kidnapped Adelaide, whom he married, making him King of Lombardy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Jan Zizka.
question.text: Zizka was a military commander of this pre-Reformation Czech religious group in a series of their namesake "wars." They followed a man who was burned at the stake in 1415.
question.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

swap.text: In the less-famous First Defenestration of Prague, seven city council members were killed by followers of this Czech religious reformer, who was condemned to death at the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: This man's teachings were heavily influenced by those of John Wycliffe, although because of this he was convicted of heresy and burned at the stake at the Council of Constance.

question.leadin: This man may have helped complete Odo of Metz's designs for a palace in Aachen, and he once dispatched a servant to pilfer holy remains from Rome to increase the piety of churches he founded.
question.text: Identify this colleague of Alcuin, a preeminent Frankish biographer from the eighth and ninth centuries.
question.clue: The preface to this notoriously short man's most famous work was written by Walafrid Strabo.

swap.text: In 1535, Suleiman lost Tunis to this Holy Roman Emperor, the son of Philip I and Joanna of Castille.
swap.clue: His general Charles of Lannoy secured the Treaty of Madrid for this man by defeating Francis I at Pavia.

question.text: The 983 revolt was faced by the second emperor with this name. Margrave Gero, who campaigned against the Wends, served the first emperor with this name who was crowned by Pope John XII in 962.
question.answerHtml: Otto [accept Otto II or Otto I; accept Otto the Great]
question.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

swap.text: Eugene of Savoy and the Duke of Marlborough also won this battle that knocked Bavaria out of the war. The Duc of Tallard was captured at this battle.
swap.clue: The major mistake of the losing side was the excessive requisitioning of troops into the namesake city.

question.text: The Count of Tilly had an earlier victory at the Battle of White Mountain in this region. A revolt in this region initiated the Thirty Years War.
question.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

swap.leadin: This group was led by Philip the Magnanimous of Hesse and John Frederick of Saxony.
swap.text: Name this alliance of Lutheran princes, mostly located within northern Germany. It eventually fought a namesake war with the Holy Roman Empire and Charles V in the 1540's.
swap.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

question.text: The Prague groschen silver currency served as the model for a similar groschen issued from Meissen by a holder of this title. Holders of this general title were originally military governors of border provinces in the Holy Roman Empire.
question.answerHtml: margrave [accept Margrave of Meissen; accept Margraviate of Meissen; accept markgraf in place of “margrave”]

swap.leadin: Many Frenchmen considered this statement to be tantamount to declaring war on France.
swap.text: Name this declaration, which was signed by Frederick William II and pledged to support Louis XVI in the face of the French Revolution.
swap.clue: This document issued in 1791 shortly after the Padua Circular.

question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor was the nominal leader of the allied army against Philip at Bouvines. He was also the only Holy Roman Emperor from the House of Welf and was succeeded upon losing at Bouvines by Frederick II.
question.clue: This Holy Roman Emperor who struggled for control over the Holy Roman Empire with Frederick II Hohenstaufen ("HO-en-shtow-fin"). He was deposed following his defeat at the Battle of Bouvines.

swap.text: The diary of mercenary Peter Hagendorf details his participation in the sack of Magdeburg, as well as this 1634 battle where the Catholic forces of Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand and Ferdinand of Hungary defeated the Protestants under Gustav Horn.
swap.clue: This 1634 battle crushed the momentum of Protestant forces under Swedish leadership. In this battle, Habsburg forces under Ferdinand III and the Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand defeated the League of Heilbronn and captured Gustav Horn.

question.leadin: John George of Saxony was one of the electors who opposed it. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this 1629 decree, in which Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II called for secularized bishoprics, such as Bremen, to be placed back under the control of the Catholic Church.
question.clue: Maximilian von Trautmannsdorf's Points of Pirna attempted to reconcile one party who had been alienated by this declaration, which was defended vociferously in Paul Laymann's Pacis Composito.

swap.leadin: Name the following battles of Gustavus Adolphus FTPE.
swap.text: In this 1631 battle, Adolphus led the Protestant forces to their first victory in the Thirty Years War.
swap.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.
